title_en: 'Being in That Suit, I Just Felt Like It Was Really Stupid to Talk Normally' — Christian Bale Reveals How His Iconic Batman Voice Was a Last-Minute Choice
summary_en: Christian Bale has revealed why he improvised his iconic gravelly Batman voice at the last minute during his Batman Begins audition with Christopher Nolan.
body_en:
Christian Bale has revealed why he improvised his iconic gravelly Batman voice at the last minute during his Batman Begins audition with Christopher Nolan.
Rather than the throat-shredding performance being something Bale had practiced beforehand, the American Psycho and Big Short star has admitted that he simply took a gamble on the voice while in the moment — and after beginning to feel self-conscious about how his natural tone sounded emanating from the Batsuit.
"Being in that suit, I just felt like it was really stupid just to talk normally," Bale explained while appearing on The Rich Eisen Show , adding that he had been given Val Kilmer's ill-fitting cast-off for purposes of the audition. Kilmer, of course, starred as Batman in the 1995 entry Batman Forver — meaning the costume was a decade old by the time Bale pulled it on.
"And so on the day I went 'ah, they're going to hate it but I'm going to go for it.' And I started doing this more bestial guttural voice. I went back home and showed my wife what I'd done and she said 'well, you've blown that one, haven't you?'"
On the contrary, however, Bale said he later discovered that "Chris Nolan... loved it," and the rest is history. Bale went on to be cast as Batman for the director's acclaimed Dark Knight trilogy. Nolan even added another husky mouthbreather for its third entry, as fellow British actor Tom Hardy left audiences looking for the subtitles during his scenes as Bane.
"I'm running around, a grown man dressed as a bat in rubber," Bale recalled of his audition. "I can't just talk like I'm hanging out. There's got be something deeper and darker and more monstrous to make this work."
In the years since, Bale's take on Batman's voice has become "iconic" — and that's according to Robert Pattinson, the current Bat, who told GQ that it had been "almost impossible" for him not to do similar when picking up the cowl, even though he had found it difficult to maintain during extended dialogue scenes. "It's so kind of iconic, the voice he was doing in it," Pattinson said. "[And] it's really, really hard."
Pattinson is next set to appear as the Dark Knight in the upcoming The Batman: Part 2, which will now launch in February 2028. While not confirmed, Pattinson's new commitment to James Bond could end his run as the DC Comics hero, meaning someone else will have to cough up their own take on Batman's voice in the not-too-distant future.
